name: News explainer carousel (GM house style)
made_from: work/_research/us-locked-out (frozen 2026-08-31) — derived from the piece's own artifacts

reference.note: palette and layout grammar sampled from @collab.gm.marketshq's published post, not invented

ladder.job: a flat statement or question about something the reader half-knows
the one sourced figure, as a table, with the reader's own row painted
ladder.figure: none — the data is the picture

ladder.job: how it works, in causal steps
a real nameable entity and what happened to it
a question the account would read the answers to

ingredients.figure_model: gpt-image-2 via pipeline/gen_figures.py (locked STYLE string, transparent background, alpha-trimmed)
rules: headlines alone must deliver the complete idea
green marks the punch words only (*asterisks* in the script)
no hashtags, no link on a slide, one product mention at most
every figure on a slide carries an evidence id

parameters.name: topic
parameters.plain: the thing in the news this one is about

parameters.name: chips
parameters.plain: the five short labels above each headline

parameters.name: figure_subjects
parameters.plain: one statue subject per slide, in the locked style

parameters.name: reader_row
parameters.plain: the row to paint in the proof table — where the reader lives

cost_per_run.figures: 4 x gpt-image-2 (~5.5k image output tokens each)
cost_per_run.note: words and layout are free; the only spend is the figures

ladder_test: Did you know there's a US stock market Americans can't touch?
Apple and Nvidia sell in 110 countries, but not in the one they're from.
An old American rule says shares sold abroad are never registered, so they can't be sold back home.
The exchange selling them went and got its licence in Abu Dhabi instead.
So if Americans aren't allowed to buy it, does that make you careful, or curious?
